summary: The sample implements a FastAPI service that builds a $facet aggregation (diagnosis, age bands via $bucket, gender, region), materializes cached summaries into an aggregations_cache collection (TTL index), exposes endpoints to read and refresh cached summaries, and includes an idempotent seed script and unit tests. Verification steps (pip install, pytest, seed, live aggregation, upsert, TTL index creation, and an explain via the DocumentDB MCP explain tool) were executed and recorded. Main issues: missing env settings in .env.example, lack of retry/backoff around network calls, seed uses per-document upserts instead of batched bulk writes, no use of $setOnInsert for creation-time metadata so createdAt is overwritten on every refresh, and some index/index-shape guidance (compound indexes / pre-filters) is not followed leading to the explain showing a COLLSCAN for the current pipeline. Several decisions were made from model defaults (Python minor, scheduler frequency) without an explicit public source; these are noted as documentation gaps the product team should author. See requirement_results, practice checks, decision_reviews and doc_gaps below.

checks.practice: Create indexes on fields used in aggregation $match or $group predicates in production workloads (index single fields when appropriate).
checks.evidence: app/seed.py lines 33-38 create indexes on patient_id (unique), diagnoses, gender, region, age. The app's seed created the indexes before upserting documents.

checks.practice: When building compound indexes, order keys by query selectivity and sort usage following ESR (Equality → Sort → Range).
checks.evidence: app/seed.py creates single-field indexes (diagnoses, gender, region, age) but does not create compound indexes. The explain captured (events.jsonl) shows the facet pipeline used a COLLSCAN on the seeded dataset.
checks.fix: Add compound indexes for common query shapes (e.g., {region:1, age:1} or {gender:1, age:1} depending on expected filters) and re-run explain; document in README how to tune indexes for production.

checks.practice: Use a TTL index on a Date field (e.g., expiresAt) with expireAfterSeconds=0 to implement absolute expiry of cached summary documents.
checks.evidence: app/create_cache_index.py line 5 creates cache.create_index([('expiresAt', 1)], expireAfterSeconds=0) and app/main.py startup_event line 38 also creates this TTL index.

checks.practice: When materializing expensive aggregations, upsert the summary document with an idempotent update (use updateOne(filter, {$set: ...}, upsert=True) or equivalent) so retries or restarts do not create duplicates.
checks.evidence: app/aggregations.py lines 83-97 compute a deterministically hashed key (_params_hash) and call cache_coll.update_one({'_id': key}, {'$set': doc}, upsert=True).
checks.source: Updating data in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB

sources.title: Updating data in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB

checks.practice: Wrap network and operation calls with retries using exponential backoff and jitter, and retry on transient errors (network errors, MongoNetworkError, socket timeouts, and 429 TooManyRequests) with a bounded max retry count.
checks.evidence: No retry/backoff wrapper is present around compute_facets or upsert_summary (app/aggregations.py lines 73-80 and 83-97); refresh_default_summary (app/main.py lines 50-61) catches Exception and prints, but does not retry transient errors with backoff.
checks.fix: Wrap aggregation and upsert calls using a retry decorator (exponential backoff + jitter) or use a retry helper from a library (e.g., tenacity) and retry on MongoNetworkError and 429 responses; make max retries configurable.

checks.practice: For large or memory-heavy aggregation pipelines enable allowDiskUse (allowDiskUse=True) so the server can spill to disk as needed.
checks.evidence: app/aggregations.py line 77 calls patients_coll.aggregate(pipeline, allowDiskUse=False). For potentially heavy faceted aggregations, allowDiskUse should be True or configurable.
checks.fix: Change to collection.aggregate(pipeline, allowDiskUse=True) or make allowDiskUse configurable by env var for the sample.

checks.practice: Design aggregation pipelines to filter and project early (place $match early, then $project to remove unused fields) so subsequent heavy stages (group, facet, sort) operate on fewer documents.
checks.evidence: app/aggregations.py build_facet_pipeline appends a $match stage (line 40) before the $facet (line 42), so upstream filtering is applied when params exist.

checks.practice: Use explain('executionStats') on representative aggregation pipelines to confirm the plan uses IXSCAN rather than COLLSCAN and to inspect keysExamined / docsExamined ratios; include this in reviews/CI for critical queries.
checks.evidence: Events show documentdb_explain_operation was invoked (events.jsonl line ~57) for the facet pipeline and returned an explain; builder recorded that explain showed a COLLSCAN in build report.

checks.practice: When materializing caches include metadata fields such as params, createdAt/created_at, expiresAt and duration_ms so refresh jobs and operators can reason about staleness and duration.
checks.evidence: app/aggregations.py upsert_summary (lines 84-94) stores params, createdAt, expiresAt and summary. duration_ms is not set.
checks.source: Aggregation pipeline guidance and update/upsert docs
checks.fix: Record duration_ms (e.g., time taken by compute_facets) and include it in the stored doc so operators can monitor refresh cost.

sources.title: Aggregation pipeline guidance and update/upsert docs

checks.practice: Use $setOnInsert with upsert operations to set creation-time metadata only on insert, keeping updates idempotent.
checks.evidence: app/aggregations.py upsert_summary (lines 86-96) uses update_one({'_id': key}, {'$set': doc}, upsert=True) which overwrites createdAt on every refresh instead of using $setOnInsert.
checks.fix: Use update_one({'_id': key}, {'$set': {'summary': summary, 'expiresAt': expires_at}, '$setOnInsert': {'createdAt': now, 'name': name, 'params': params}}, upsert=True) so createdAt is set only on insert.

checks.practice: When seeding or bulk-loading data, use batched inserts (e.g., groups of 500–2000 documents) or bulkWrite to reduce overhead and RU charge compared to many single inserts.
checks.evidence: app/seed.py lines 41-46 upsert one document per loop via update_one; no batching or bulkWrite is performed.
checks.source: Optimize write performance / bulk writes (Azure DocumentDB guidance)
checks.fix: Use insert_many or bulk_write in batches (e.g., collect 500 docs then bulk_write with upsert operations) to reduce per-document overhead; make batch size configurable.

sources.title: Optimize write performance / bulk writes (Azure DocumentDB guidance)

checks.practice: Prefer pre-aggregating high-cost summaries (materialized cached documents) for faceted dashboards and refresh them on a schedule or on-change rather than running full aggregations on every HTTP request.
checks.evidence: app/main.py GET /facets supports use_cache and reads/writes cached summaries (lines 63-81). refresh_default_summary refreshes cache hourly.

checks.practice: Use the provided tooling (DocumentDB MCP server / VS Code extension) to inspect collections, indexes, and explain plans when validating what the app created.
checks.evidence: Events show documentdb_explain_operation was invoked (events.jsonl) and the builder reported capturing the explain plan in the build report.

decision_reviews.comment: Approval with readiness 'ready_with_gaps' is an operator-level decision; the run shows verification performed and gaps documented, so this decision is sound.
Choosing Python + FastAPI follows the explicit starter prompt. Events and files show FastAPI code present, so the decision aligns with the prompt.

Choosing Python 3.11 is a model_default decision (reason_source=model_default). No public source in the run explicitly required 3.11; this is a reasonable choice but not grounded in a public doc, so it is unverifiable from available evidence. (Readiness findings flagged Python minor version as an information gap.)

Decision to use a singleton MongoClient is supported by the documentdb-driver skill and the code (app/db.py) implements it. Events show the documentdb-driver skill was loaded, matching the reason_source='skill'.

Choosing APScheduler as an in-process scheduler is a model_default decision. The app implements APScheduler (app/main.py). The choice is defensible for a sample, but the reason is model_default and not directly grounded in a public guidance page—mark as unverifiable.
Choice of database name 'sample_healthcare_16' follows the run-environment instruction. The code uses that database (app/db.py default) and the seed/collections reference it via get_db().

Choosing to seed 5,000 records is a model_default decision. It is reasonable and the seed was executed successfully, but it's not grounded in an explicit public requirement—so unverifiable as a documented policy decision.

Creating single-field indexes plus a TTL index is supported by the documentdb-indexing skill and the repo: app/seed.py creates the indexes and app/create_cache_index.py constructs the TTL index. The events show the index creation and the TTL index script was run.
The one-hour refresh schedule is a model_default choice (reason_source=model_default). It's sensible for a demo but not grounded in a public doc; the code implements hourly scheduling (app/main.py).

Decision to install dependencies to run tests was logged as reason_source='tool_unavailable'; events show pytest was not found, pip install -r requirements.txt executed successfully and then pytest ran. The event trace supports the decision.
Decision to run the seed script now is grounded in the prompt/run-environment and events show python seed.py --count 5000 was executed successfully; the choice and evidence are consistent.
Decision to run a live aggregation to verify the pipeline is supported by events (python run_query.py produced bucket outputs) and by readiness guidance. The decision and its evidence are coherent.
Upserting the computed summary into aggregations_cache was performed (store_summary.py executed) and matches the skill guidance; events show the upsert succeeded.
Creating the TTL index via script was logged and executed (create_cache_index.py run); the decision and event trace align with skill guidance for TTL indexes.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The repository's .env.example only contains DOCUMENTDB_URI. The sample expects and uses other configurable values (cache name, TTL, refresh schedule, optional pool sizing), but those are not listed.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Inspected repo files (.env.example, README) and discovery searches for 'env example refresh schedule SUMMARY_NAME TTL_SECONDS'.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Developers must manually know these settings; the builder used sensible defaults in code (DEFAULT_SUMMARY_NAME, TTL_SECONDS, hourly refresh) rather than exposing them as env-configurable. This makes reproducing different schedules or cache names harder.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add to .env.example and README entries: REFRESH_HOURS=1, SUMMARY_NAME=default_cohort, TTL_SECONDS=86400, MAX_POOL_SIZE=100, SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS=20000, RETRY_WRITES=false (or instruction that retryWrites is set in the connection string). Document what each does and defaults used in code.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No clear public, discoverable mapping in the repo that tells which pymongo version is recommended for the cluster wire-protocol/serverVersion targeted by the sample (the repo pins pymongo==4.5.0 but no rationale is present).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Searched Microsoft Learn and installed skills for 'supported pymongo versions' and 'driver compatibility' but did not find a single, agent-friendly table mapping client driver versions to cluster serverVersion.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample pins a driver version; an agent or user might pick an incompatible version for a particular cluster serverVersion. This risks runtime errors on some clusters.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short Learn quickstart section or a line in the documentdb-driver skill that lists recommended driver versions (pymongo) for each supported serverVersion and known incompatibilities. Example: 'If cluster serverVersion=7.0, use pymongo >=4.4 and tested with 4.5.0'.

doc_gaps.topic: Guidance for scheduler choice and refresh frequency
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No public guidance in the skills or quickstarts recommends in-process APScheduler vs an external scheduled job (Functions/Logic Apps) or which default refresh frequency suits which workloads.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-connection, documentdb-data-modeling, general operational guidance and README; no authoritative instruction on choosing scheduler patterns for demo vs production.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder chose an in-process APScheduler hourly refresh by default. That choice is reasonable for a sample but may be inadequate for production (observability, retries, scaling).
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add an agent-kit rule: 'For samples, prefer in-process scheduler when demonstrating behaviour only; add a README callout that production deployments should use an external scheduled job or serverless function; include an example Azure Function-based refresh in infra examples.'

doc_gaps.topic: DocumentDB guidance for materialized cache id naming
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No public advice was found about naming conventions for deterministic cache document _id values for materialized summaries (what keys to include to guarantee idempotence and cache locality).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Searched for 'deterministic cache _id materialized summary best practice' and similar phrases; discovery recorded no useful public hits.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder implemented a SHA256 of (name, params) which is reasonable, but agents may choose non-deterministic ids or naive UUIDs without guidance, breaking upserts and causing duplicate cache entries.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short doc section 'Materialized summary id recommendations' recommending deterministic keys (hash of canonicalized params + summary name), examples in Python and how to handle param ordering, TTL, and collision considerations.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No authoritative public guidance found that recommends a test database name or teardown approach for DocumentDB sample tests (e.g., whether to use a separate 'sample_healthcare_16_test' DB and automated cleanup).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Searched for 'DocumentDB testing separate test database tear down tests sample_healthcare_16_test' and related queries; no clear public best-practice was found.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample's unit tests are pure-Python and run without a cluster, but there is no pattern or helper for integration tests that would seed/tear-down a test DB; builders may be uncertain how to add integration tests safely.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a small 'Testing and CI' page: recommend using a separate test database name (e.g., <sample>_test), provide an optional test_seed.py that creates and drops test DB collections, and example CI snippets that require an env var TEST_DOCUMENTDB_URI pointed at a throwaway cluster.

doc_gaps.topic: Model-default decisions (Python minor, seed size, hourly refresh)
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Several builder choices were made from model defaults rather than public guidance: Python minor version selection (3.11), seed size (5000), and default refresh frequency (1 hour).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Readiness notes and decision logs; searches for explicit recommended defaults did not yield a single 'for samples use X' page.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: These defaults are reasonable for a sample but inconsistent or undocumented defaults across samples can confuse users and agents.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add an Agent Kit rule file stating recommended defaults for gallery samples (target Python minor, seed sizes for small/medium/large demos, and recommended demo refresh frequencies), and suggest doc locations to override.

doc_gaps.topic: Public guidance to prefer $setOnInsert on upserts
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Although the $setOnInsert operator exists in public docs, sample-level guidance to prefer using $setOnInsert when creating cache documents was not explicit in the repository's README.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Repo README and skills resources; $setOnInsert docs exist but no sample snippet used it.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The upsert implementation currently overwrites createdAt on every refresh which loses insert-time metadata; this is a small correctness issue easily fixed, but an explicit sample guidance would prevent the mistake.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short 'Materialized cache upsert pattern' in the README showing an example use of update_one(..., {'$set': {...}, '$setOnInsert': {...}}, upsert=True).
